name: nf-core/dualrnaseq
description: **nf-core/dualrnaseq** is a bioinformatics pipeline built using [Nextflow](https://www.nextflow.io), a workflow tool to run tasks across multiple compute infrastructures in a very portable manner. It comes with docker containers making installation trivial and results highly reproducible

name: nf-core/eager
description: **nf-core/eager** is a scalable and reproducible bioinformatics best-practise processing pipeline for genomic NGS sequencing data, with a focus on ancient DNA (aDNA) data. It is ideal for the (palaeo)genomic analysis of humans, animals, plants, microbes and even microbiomes

name: nf-core/epitopeprediction
description: **nf-core/epitopeprediction** is a bioinformatics best-practice analysis pipeline for epitope prediction and annotation. The pipeline performs epitope predictions for a given set of variants, proteins, or peptides directly using state of the art prediction tools. The pipeline can be used to generate putative neo-epitopes with variant input, scan one or more proteins for binding hotspots or darkspots analysis, and perform binding predictions on immunopeptidomics data with peptide input

name: nf-core/evexplorer

name: nf-core/fastqrepair
description: **nf-core/fastqrepair** is a bioinformatics pipeline that can be used to recover corrupted `FASTQ.gz` files, drop or fix uncompliant reads, remove unpaired reads, and settles reads that became disordered. It takes a `samplesheet` with FASTQ/FASTQ.gz files as input (both single-end and paired-end) and produces clean FASTQ files and QC reports

name: nf-core/fastquorum
description: **nf-core/fastquorum** is a bioinformatics pipeline that implements the pipeline implements the [fgbio Best Practices FASTQ to Consensus Pipeline][fgbio-best-practices-link] to produce consensus reads using unique molecular indexes/barcodes (UMIs). `nf-core/fastquorum` can produce consensus reads from single or multi UMI reads, and even [Duplex Sequencing][duplex-seq-link] reads

name: nf-core/fetchngs
description: **nf-core/fetchngs** is a bioinformatics pipeline to fetch metadata and raw FastQ files from both public databases. At present, the pipeline supports SRA / ENA / DDBJ / GEO ids (see [usage docs](https://nf-co.re/fetchngs/usage#introduction))

name: nf-core/funcscan
description: **nf-core/funcscan** is a bioinformatics best-practice analysis pipeline for the screening of nucleotide sequences such as assembled contigs for functional genes. It currently features mining for antimicrobial peptides, antibiotic resistance genes and biosynthetic gene clusters

name: nf-core/genephylo
description: Complete this sentence with a 2-3 sentence summary of what types of data the pipeline ingests, a brief overview of the major pipeline sections and the types of output it produces. You're giving an overview to someone new to nf-core here, in 15-20 seconds. For an example, see https://github.com/nf-core/rnaseq/blob/master/README.md#introduction -->.

name: nf-core/genephylomodeler
description: **nf-core/genephylomodeler** is a bioinformatics pipeline that fits evolutionary models and performs hypothesis testing on multiple sequence alignments of coding genes. These include (but are not limited to) detecting signatures of selection and estimating evolutionary rates using methods from HyPhy, PAML, and other packages. The pipeline takes a samplesheet with alignment files and phylogenetic trees as input, applies one or more tools of interest, and produces an output in JSON and text format.

name: nf-core/genomeannotator
description: Genome annotation pipeline: predict genes, transposable elements, and non-coding RNA from assembled genomes using MAKER, AUGUSTUS, and RepeatModeler

name: nf-core/genomeassembler

Steps: LigPrep (protonation, tautomers, stereochemistry) -> Protein Preparation Wizard (H-bond assignment, restrained minimisation) -> Grid Generation (inner/outer box, van der Waals scaling) -> Glide docking (HTVS/SP/XP precision, GlideScore, E_model, LipophilicEvolution) -> ranked SDF + HTML report. Precision: HTVS (fast), SP (standard), XP (extra precision, most accurate). License: Schrodinger FlexNet (SCHRODINGER_LICENSE_FILE=27008@host, user must provide). Container: ECR schrodinger2024.

name: AMBER pmemd GPU Molecular Dynamics
description: AMBER pmemd.cuda GPU-accelerated MD simulation pipeline for protein-ligand systems. Steps: GAFF2 ligand parametrization antechamber parmchk2 -> tleap complex build -> 2-stage energy minimisation sander -> NVT NPT equilibration pmemd.cuda -> production MD simulation pmemd.cuda -> cpptraj trajectory analysis RMSD RMSF Rg -> MMPBSA.py MM-GBSA MMGBSA binding free energy ΔGbind ~-9 kcal/mol. License: free academic AMBER24 license agreement. Container: ECR amber24-cuda.

name: MOE Covalent Docking Pipeline
description: MOE (Molecular Operating Environment) covalent docking pipeline for irreversible and reversible covalent inhibitors. Steps: LigPrep (tautomers, protonation, MMFF94x charges) -> QuickPrep receptor prep (Protonate3D, restrained minimisation) -> CovDock SVL (explicit covalent bond to CYS/LYS/SER/THR/HIS) -> S score + GBVI/WSA dG rescoring -> SDF export + HTML report. Warhead types: acrylamide, chloroacetamide, epoxide, aldehyde, michael_acceptor, vinyl_sulfone, boronic_acid. License: MOE FlexNet (LM_LICENSE_FILE=27001@host, user must provide). Container: ECR moe2024.

name: Pharmacophore Filtering
description: drug_discovery/pharmacophore_filtering Pharmacophore-based compound library filtering pipeline Pipeline Steps: 1. PHARMACOPHORE_GENERATE — Derive a consensus pharmacophore model from known active SMILES; identifies the most common Donor (D), Acceptor (A), Aromatic (Ar), Hydrophobic (H), and PosIonizable (P) features via RDKit's chemical feature factory (live) or hardcoded rules (mock). 2. PHARMACOPHORE_SCREEN   — Score each compound in a SMILES/SDF library by number of pharmacophore features mat

name: Pocket Detection Druggability
description: drug_discovery/pocket_detection_druggability Sprint: fpocket-based binding-site detection and druggability assessment Pipeline Steps: 1. FPOCKET_POCKET_DETECTION   — Detect binding cavities in a PDB structure; score each pocket by volume (Å³), druggability score (0–1), hydrophobicity index, and polarity fraction 2. DRUGGABILITY_QC_GATE       — Evidence-graded QC gate: PASS if best_pocket druggability_score ≥ min_druggability AND volume ≥ min_volume WARN if druggability_score ≥ warn_druggability

name: Aizynthfinder Retrosynthesis
description: drug_discovery/aizynthfinder_retrosynthesis Retrosynthesis of drug-like small molecules using AiZynthFinder (AstraZeneca open-source CASP tool — https://github.com/MolecularAI/aizynthfinder) Inputs: smiles_list  — channel of SMILES strings (one per compound) mock_mode    — boolean (default true); synthetic data, no AiZynthFinder needed max_routes   — max synthesis routes per compound (params, default 5) max_depth    — max retrosynthesis tree depth (params, default 6) Outputs (emitted channels):

name: Drug Moa Rnaseq
description: drug_discovery/drug_moa_rnaseq Drug Mechanism-of-Action (MoA) Characterisation from RNA-seq Data. Fills Gap 9 in BioMate's drug discovery opportunity analysis. Pipeline Steps: 1. DIFFERENTIAL_EXPRESSION — Identify significantly DE genes between drug-treated and control samples using DESeq2 (live) or seeded synthetic data (mock); outputs ranked gene TSV and volcano JSON. 2. GENE_SET_ENRICHMENT    — Run GSEA against MSigDB Hallmark gene sets (fgsea live; synthetic NES scores mock). Identifies enri

name: Saposin Nanodisc SPA
description: CryoSPARC SPA pipeline optimized for small membrane proteins (< 60 kDa) reconstituted in saposin A nanodisc. Uses 0.649 A/pix (mandatory for < 60 kDa), 60 e-/A2 dose, 256 px box size. Includes saposin reconstitution QC gate (NS-EM nanodisc size ~10 nm, SEC single symmetric peak) before cryo-EM. TOPAZ training pass after initial blob-pick 2D classification. Protocol: saposin + gamma-cyclodextrin lipid delivery, Bio-Beads detergent removal, UltrAuFoil blot 1.5s at 10C.

name: GPCR Complex SPA
description: CryoSPARC SPA pipeline for GPCR-G protein complexes in MSP nanodisc (MSP1D1DeltaH5). Uses 0.83 A/pix for 100-150 kDa complexes. Includes GPCR complex assembly QC: SEC stoichiometry, scFv16 stabilizer confirmation, nucleotide-free check after apyrase treatment. Assembly: Sf9 baculovirus, apyrase nucleotide removal, scFv16 (mandatory for Gi complexes), MSP1D1DeltaH5 nanodisc. Dual local refinement: TM bundle + G protein masks. Supports Gi, Gs, Gq, G11 G protein types.

name: Multi Drug Atlas
description: Multi-drug pharmacology SPA pipeline with drug difference map analysis. Processes apo + N drug-bound datasets through identical SPA pipelines, generates difference maps (drug minus apo, plus minus 3 sigma threshold). Validates ligand density occupancy. Outputs drug atlas comparison report. Designed for ion channel multi-drug pharmacology (CaV1.2 seven-drug atlas) and GPCR multi-PAM cooperativity. All datasets must share identical pixel_size, defocus, and dose for valid subtraction.

name: DeepEMhancer Post-Processing
description: DeepEMhancer deep learning map sharpening and density enhancement. Automatically selects model (tight/wide/highRes) based on achieved resolution. Input: half-map pair (.mrc). Output: enhanced map with improved local resolution, particularly at flexible regions. Runs in mock mode without GPU. Alternative to B-factor sharpening for heterogeneous local resolution.

name: Liposome Pore Forming SPA
description: CryoSPARC SPA for pore-forming proteins (BAX, gasdermin, perforin, VDAC) reconstituted in liposomes. Includes mandatory ANTS/DPX lysis assay gate (>50% lysis required before cryo-EM). Cardiolipin mandatory for BAX-family pores. DDM sub-CMC extraction step for SPA sample preparation. Protocol: POPC:POPE:CL liposomes -> pore activation -> lysis assay -> DDM extraction -> SPA. Reference: BAX pore Science 2025 (Shi lab).

name: RELION Multi-Body Refinement
description: RELION 3D multi-body refinement for large flexible complexes (spliceosome, ribosome, GroEL, nuclear pore complex). Decomposes complex into N rigid bodies, refines each independently while maintaining relative positions. PCA analysis of body motions reveals principal conformational modes. Per-body FSC validates local resolution improvement. Input: RELION particles STAR file + consensus map + N soft body masks. Reference: Nakane et al. 2018 eLife (RELION multibody).

name: Assay Ingestion And Ranking
description: drug_discovery/assay_ingestion_and_ranking Ingest multi-assay compound data and produce a composite safety-potency ranking. Pipeline Steps: 1. PARSE_ASSAY_DATA -- Parse CSV assay data, validate required columns, pivot to wide format. 2. COMPUTE_COMPOSITE_SCORE -- Normalise BCR-ABL1 IC50 (potency) and hERG IC50 (safety), compute weighted composite score. 3. RANK_AND_REPORT -- Sort compounds by composite score, emit ranked CSV + HTML report + JSON summary.

name: Cro Submission Export
description: drug_discovery/cro_submission_export Format top-N compounds for CRO submission in WuXi AppTec standard format. Pipeline Steps: 1. VALIDATE_COMPOUNDS -- Safety validation: hERG IC50 > threshold, exclude unsafe compounds. 2. FORMAT_CRO_SUBMISSION -- Add MW and LogP from SMILES (RDKit), format WuXi AppTec required columns. 3. EXPORT_CSV -- Write final submission CSV + metadata JSON + summary report.

name: P0 Docking Validation
description: drug_discovery/p0_docking_validation Phase 0 internal validation: AutoDock Vina vs published crystal structure. Protocol: 1. Download receptor PDB from RCSB (default: 7RFS - Mpro + nirmatrelvir) 2. Extract reference ligand from crystal structure 3. Prepare receptor PDBQT (meeko) 4. Prepare ligand PDBQT from SMILES (meeko + RDKit ETKDG) 5. Run AutoDock Vina (exhaustiveness=16 for validation) 6. Compute RMSD top-1 pose vs crystal coordinates (heavy atoms) 7. PASS if RMSD <= 2.0 Angstrom AND at lea

name: P0 Mrna Validation
description: drug_discovery/p0_mrna_validation Phase 0 internal validation: mRNA codon optimisation + structure prediction. Protocol (P0-B from study proposal): 1. Fetch SARS-CoV-2 spike protein ORF from GenBank (MN908947.3 nt 21563-25384) or use provided sequence 2. Apply hexapro stabilising mutations (K986P, V987P, F817P, A892P, A899P, A942P) on amino acid level, then back-translate with human codon optimisation 3. Add 5'-UTR (human beta-globin, Kozak), signal peptide, 3'-UTR 4. Calculate Codon Adaptation

name: Crispr Screen Mageck
description: genomics/crispr_screen_mageck Pooled CRISPR screen analysis using MAGeCK (Model-based Analysis of Genome-wide CRISPR Knockout). Supports both loss-of-function (negative selection) and gain-of-function (positive selection) screens. Runs the full MAGeCK pipeline: count → test → pathway enrichment. Outputs: mageck_count/         — per-guide read counts across all samples mageck_test/          — gene-level RRA scores, p-values, FDR (pos + neg selection) pathway_enrichment/   — GSEA on MAGeCK gene sc

name: Lc Ms Proteomics Metabolomics
description: multi_omics/lc_ms_proteomics_metabolomics Integrated LC-MS/MS proteomics + untargeted metabolomics analysis. Covers two instrument modes in a single workflow: DDA/DIA proteomics  — MaxQuant (DDA) or DIA-NN (DIA) → differential abundance (MSstats) Untargeted metabolomics — XCMS peak picking → putative annotation (HMDB/KEGG) → DA Joint output: Multi-omics integration: protein–metabolite correlation network (Pearson |r| > 0.7), shared pathway enrichment (ORA on KEGG), and a joint HTML report. Outpu

name: Admet Pred
description: pharmacology/ADMET_pred ADMET (Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, Toxicity) safety screening. Uses RDKit molecular descriptors to estimate: - hERG IC50 (μM): Aronov 2008 J Med Chem 51:6632 logP-based model - DILI risk: Lammert et al. 2010 Toxicol Sci lipophilicity + MW model Always produces toxicity_report.json with structured QC-gate-ready fields. nf-core style module generated from tested Galaxy wrapper.

name: Apply Vcog Grade
description: Apply VCOG-CTCAE grading criteria to an adverse event. 1-step pipeline: APPLY_VCOG_GRADE. Outputs: json, txt. Key parameters: event_type, severity_value, species, symptom.

name: Docking Autodock Vina
description: pharmacology/docking_autodock_vina Real AutoDock Vina molecular docking pipeline. Steps: 1. Prepare receptor: strip water/heteroatoms, add H, write PDBQT (uses meeko MoleculePreparation or openbabel fallback) 2. Prepare ligand(s): convert SMILES -> 3D SDF -> PDBQT via meeko 3. Run AutoDock Vina for each ligand 4. Parse best binding affinity (kcal/mol) + RMSD from top pose 5. If reference_ligand_pdbqt provided: compute RMSD vs crystal pose (validation mode for P0-C: should be <= 2.0 A for success

name: Ivive Hepatic Clearance
description: pharmacology/ivive_hepatic_clearance In vitro to in vivo extrapolation (IVIVE) of hepatic clearance. Scales microsomal or hepatocyte CLint to predicted in vivo hepatic clearance (CLh) using the well-stirred liver model (Wilkinson & Shand 1975 Clin Pharmacol Ther 18:377; Obach 1999 Drug Metab Dispos 27:1350). Supports: - Microsomal CLint (μL/min/mg protein) scaled via MPPGL - Hepatocyte CLint (μL/min/10⁶ cells) scaled via hepatocellularity - Species: human, rat, mouse, dog Outputs ivive_results.j

name: Predict Admet Properties
description: pharmacology/predict_admet_properties Predicts ADMET (Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, Toxicity) properties for a list of compounds using: 1. RDKit molecular descriptors (hERG IC50 estimate, DILI risk) — always runs 2. DeepPurpose MPNN/CNN/Morgan pretrained models (ClinTox, solubility, etc.) — optional; runs when DeepPurpose is installed in the container. Always produces toxicity_report.json with structured QC-gate-ready fields. nf-core style module generated from tested Galaxy w

name: P0 Pharmacophore Validation
description: drug_discovery/p0_pharmacophore_validation Phase 0 internal validation: pharmacophore enrichment vs GLP-1R actives. Protocol (P0-D from study proposal): 1. Download PDB 7KI0 (Zhang et al. Cell Reports 2021) GLP-1R + TT-OAD2 small-molecule agonist (non-peptide) 2. Extract the bound TT-OAD2 ligand and derive pharmacophore features using RDKit ChemicalFeatures (Donor, Acceptor, Aromatic, Hydrophobic) 3. Score a curated compound set against the pharmacophore: - 20 known GLP-1R small-molecule agonist

name: P0 PKPD Semaglutide Validation
description: Phase 0 PKPD validation: semaglutide 2-compartment SC PK model (Overgaard 2019) plus GLP-1R Emax body weight PD model validated against SUSTAIN-1 trial. pkpd pharmacokinetics pharmacodynamics semaglutide GLP-1R Ozempic Wegovy body weight obesity diabetes ODE simulation. Pass: Cmax within 30% of 15 nM AND weight loss -3 to -6 kg at 30 weeks.

name: HTML Output Test
description: Test workflow that generates a MultiQC-style HTML report. Used for E2E testing of the HTML iframe viewer. Runs locally with no containers required.

name: OpenFE Relative Binding Free Energy (RBFE)
description: OpenFE RBFE alchemical free energy perturbation pipeline. Calculates DDG (relative binding free energy, kcal/mol) between two ligands competing for the same protein binding site. Uses OpenFE SepTop protocol + OpenMM 8 GPU MD, Lomap2 MCS atom mapping, and Cinnabar MBAR estimator. Steps: ligand prep (OpenFF Sage 2.2) -> protein prep (PDBFixer ff14sb) -> RBFE setup (lambda windows) -> production HREX simulation -> MBAR analysis. Outputs DDG +/- SEM, overlap matrix, convergence plot, HTML report.

name: CYP450 DDI Panel + Hepatic Clearance
description: CYP450 drug-drug interaction (DDI) panel and hepatic clearance prediction. Predicts CYP inhibition IC50 (uM) for all 5 major isoforms (CYP1A2, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, CYP2D6, CYP3A4) using QSAR ML models. Scales in vitro microsomal CLint to in vivo hepatic clearance via IVIVE well-stirred model (Obach 1997). Applies FDA 2020 DDI guidance thresholds (R1, R1gut). Steps: SMILES validation -> CYP inhibition prediction -> hepatic clearance IVIVE -> DDI risk flags -> HTML report with radar chart + clearance funnel.

name: CryoSPARC Standard Single-Particle Analysis
description: CryoSPARC Standard Single-Particle Analysis (SPA) pipeline for cryo-EM datasets. 23-step modular workflow: Import Movies → Patch Motion Correction → Patch CTF Estimation → Micrograph Denoiser → Blob Picker → Junk 2D Detector → Inspect Picks → Extract Particles (2 rounds) → 2D Classification (2 rounds) → Select 2D Classes → Template Picker → Ab-Initio Reconstruction → Homogeneous Refinement → Local CTF Refinement → Non-Uniform Refinement → Local Resolution → Sharpening → Validation FSC. Suitable for soluble proteins, complexes, and ribosomes.

name: Cryo-ET Full Pipeline
description: Cryo-ET Full Pipeline — end-to-end cryo electron tomography workflow. 5 steps: Import Tilt Series → Tilt Alignment (AreTomo2/IMOD) → Tomogram Reconstruction (WBP/SIRT) → Subtomogram Averaging (STA) → Summary. All tilt series processed in parallel. Outputs: reconstructed tomograms, subtomogram average maps, alignment reports.

name: 3D Variability Pipeline
description: CryoSPARC 3D variability analysis pipeline for conformational heterogeneity in cryo-EM datasets. Identifies continuous motions and discrete conformational states.

name: Focused Refinement Pipeline
description: CryoSPARC focused refinement pipeline for improving resolution of specific regions or subunits. Useful for flexible proteins where global refinement is limited.

name: Subtomogram Averaging
description: Subtomogram averaging (STA) pipeline for in-situ structure determination from cryo-ET tomograms.

name: Helical SPA Pipeline
description: CryoSPARC Helical Single-Particle Analysis (SPA) pipeline for filamentous assemblies. 11-step workflow: Import Movies → Patch Motion Correction → Patch CTF Estimation → Filament Tracer → Extract Helical Particles → 2D Classification (helical) → Select 2D Classes → Ab-Initio Helical → Helical Refinement → Sharpening → Summary. Optimized for F-actin, amyloid fibrils, microtubules, intermediate filaments, viral tubes. Supports helical rise/twist parameter refinement.

name: boltz_structure_prediction
description: Biomolecular structure prediction using Boltz-2 (MIT licensed). Predicts structures of proteins, RNA, DNA, ligands, and protein-ligand complexes with binding affinity estimates. 1000x faster than physics-based FEP. Input: FASTA or YAML. Output: mmCIF/PDB structures, confidence scores.

name: chai1_structure_prediction
description: Multi-modal biomolecular structure prediction using Chai-1 (Apache 2.0). Handles proteins, small molecules, DNA, RNA, glycosylations, and multi-chain complexes in a single forward pass. State-of-the-art accuracy. Input: FASTA with chain type headers. Output: mmCIF structures.

name: drugclip_virtual_screening
description: Ultra-fast structure-based virtual screening using DrugCLIP (Science 2026). CLIP-based contrastive learning; 10 million times faster than docking. Screened 10K proteins x 500M compounds. Input: protein PDB + SMILES file. Output: ranked compound hits with scores.

name: scfv_antibody_design
description: AI-driven scFv intrabody design using ProteinMPNN + AlphaFold2 (Science Advances 2026). Converts conventional antibodies to functional single-chain Fv intrabodies. 73% success rate vs 31% standard methods. Input: antibody PDB. Output: designed scFv sequences (FASTA) + predicted structures.

name: syncraft_synthesizability
description: LLM-guided molecular synthesizability optimization using SynCraft. Uses Chain-of-Thought prompting with Gemini-2.5-Pro to predict atom-level edits (DEL_ATOM, ADD_BOND, DEL_BOND, CHANGE_BOND) that improve synthetic accessibility. Input: SMILES string or file. Output: optimized SMILES with SA scores.

name: protrek_protein_search
description: Trimodal protein search using ProTrek (Nature Biotechnology 2025). Unifies sequence, structure, and function through contrastive learning. Search 5B+ proteins by text description, amino acid sequence, or 3D structure. Input: text query / FASTA / PDB. Output: ranked protein hits with scores.

name: profam_fitness_prediction
description: Protein variant fitness prediction using ProFAM-1 (251M parameter autoregressive model). State-of-the-art on ProteinGym benchmark (0.47 substitutions, 0.53 indels Spearman rho). No multiple sequence alignment required at inference. Input: FASTA with variants or CSV variant table. Output: fitness scores per variant.

name: state_perturbation_prediction
description: Virtual cell perturbation prediction using STATE (Arc Institute). Predicts cellular transcriptional responses to genetic or chemical perturbations without running experiments. Trained on 270M+ cells including Tahoe-100M. Input: AnnData h5ad + perturbation name. Output: predicted expression profiles + DEGs.

name: allometric_scaling
tools_used: RDKit, SciPy, power-law regression, Rule of Exponents
description: Scales pharmacokinetic parameters (CL, Vd, t½) from preclinical species to human using allometric regression (power law), Rule of Exponents (Mahmood 2003), and MLP/brain-weight correction factors. Predicts first-in-human dose (MABEL/MRSD) per FDA 2005 Guidance. Input: JSON array of per-species PK data (rat/dog/monkey). Output: human PK prediction + FIH dose.

name: cns_penetration_prediction
tools_used: RDKit, CNS MPO (Wager 2010), Kpuu brain model (Friden 2011)
tags: CNS,blood-brain barrier,BBB,brain penetration,CNS MPO,Kpuu,P-gp,BCRP,efflux ratio,central nervous system
description: Predicts blood-brain barrier permeability and CNS drug exposure. Computes CNS MPO score (6 RDKit descriptors per Wager et al. 2010), P-gp/BCRP efflux substrate status, and Kp,uu,brain (unbound brain-to-plasma ratio). Input: SMILES (single or batch). Output: cns_properties.csv, brain_penetration.csv with BBB class (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW).

name: dart_toxicity_prediction
tools_used: RDKit, ICH S5 SMARTS alert library, placental transfer model
tags: DART,developmental toxicity,reproductive toxicity,teratogenicity,placental transfer,ICH S5,structural alerts,DMPK
description: Predicts Developmental And Reproductive Toxicity (DART) risk using structural alerts (ICH S5/OECD QSAR library, 16 alert classes) and physicochemical placental transfer model. Returns risk tier (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW), triggered alerts, and regulatory recommendations (ICH S5A/B). Input: SMILES. Output: dart_alerts.csv, placental_transfer.csv, dart_risk_tier.json.

name: oral_absorption_bcs_model
tools_used: RDKit, ESOL (Delaney 2004), Caco-2 QSAR (Hou 2004), BCS FDA 2017
description: BCS classification and oral absorption modeling. Predicts solubility (ESOL model), Caco-2 permeability (QSAR), BCS class (I-IV), dissolution profile (first-order kinetics, fed/fasted), and oral bioavailability (F%). Recommends formulation strategy (ASD, lipid-based, HCl salt, standard). Input: SMILES + dose_mg. Output: bcs_classification.json, dissolution_profile.csv, formulation_recommendation.json.

name: transporter_ddi_prediction
tools_used: RDKit, FDA DDI Basic Model 2020, Karlgren et al. transporter rules
description: Predicts substrate and inhibitor status for 8 FDA-mandated drug transporters (OATP1B1, OATP1B3, P-gp, BCRP, MATE1, MATE2-K, OAT1, OCT2). Calculates static DDI AUC ratios per FDA DDI Guidance 2020 basic model. Flags transporters requiring in vitro mechanistic studies or clinical DDI studies. Input: SMILES + Cmax_uM. Output: transporter_results.csv, regulatory_summary.json.

name: repeated_dose_tox_prediction
tools_used: RDKit, ICH M7 alerts, OECD QSAR alerts, rdkit-toxicophore
description: Predicts organ-level toxicity from repeated dosing using a structural alert library (>25 ICH M7 + OECD QSAR alerts) covering hepatotoxicity, nephrotoxicity, cardiotoxicity, and bone marrow suppression. Estimates NOAEL from alert severity and safety margin vs projected Cmax. Input: SMILES (batch), optional projected_Cmax_nM. Output: tox_alerts.csv, tox_summary.json, safety_margins.csv.

name: nanoparticle_pk_biodistribution
tools_used: SciPy ODE, EPR model (Wilhelm 2016), PEG stealth model (Arvizo 2011)
description: Models in vivo pharmacokinetics of nanoparticle-formulated drugs. 4-compartment ODE model (blood, tumor, liver/MPS, peripheral) with PEG stealth model and EPR tumor accumulation (Wilhelm et al. 2016 meta-analysis). Predicts circulation half-life, tumor EPR accumulation, MPS uptake at 24h. Input: particle_diameter_nm, surface_chemistry, PEG_density. Output: pk_profile.csv, half_life_summary.json.

name: membrane_permeability_prediction
tools_used: RDKit, Caco-2 QSAR (Hou 2004), PAMPA QSAR (Gao 2008), P-gp Seelig model
tags: Caco-2,PAMPA,membrane permeability,P-gp,efflux ratio,BCS permeability,intestinal absorption,oral bioavailability
description: Predicts apparent permeability across intestinal (Caco-2) and artificial (PAMPA) membranes. Computes P-gp/BCRP efflux substrate status, efflux ratio, and BCS permeability class. QSAR models from Hou et al. 2004 and Gao et al. 2008. Input: SMILES. Output: permeability_results.csv with Papp A→B/B→A, efflux ratio, P-gp status.

name: lnp_formulation_optimization
tools_used: RDKit, Henderson-Hasselbalch, Kulkarni LNP model, Semple formulation data
tags: LNP,lipid nanoparticle,mRNA delivery,siRNA,ionizable lipid,pKa,endosomal escape,formulation,gene therapy,nucleic acid delivery
description: Optimizes lipid nanoparticle (LNP) formulation for nucleic acid delivery (mRNA/siRNA/ASO/DNA). Predicts ionizable lipid pKa (RDKit proxy), endosomal escape score (Henderson-Hasselbalch), and tissue targeting score. Sweeps IL:helper:cholesterol:PEG-lipid molar ratios. Input: ionizable_lipid_SMILES, cargo_type, target_tissue. Output: recommended_formulation.json.

name: target_engagement_kinetics
tools_used: RDKit, SciPy ODE, Copeland kinetics model (2016)
tags: target engagement,residence time,kon,koff,receptor occupancy,kinetics,drug-target binding,RT,drug residence time
description: Estimates drug-target binding kinetic rate constants (kon, koff) and residence time (RT = 1/koff). Solves receptor occupancy ODE with time-varying drug concentration from 1-compartment PK model. Determines whether residence time is adequate for QD/BID dosing. Input: SMILES, optional IC50_nM and PK params. Output: kinetics_prediction.json, occupancy_profile.csv.

name: proteome_selectivity_profiling
tools_used: RDKit, ChEMBL REST API v3, Morgan fingerprints, Tanimoto kNN
description: Predicts binding affinity across kinase (468 kinome), GPCR, or nuclear receptor panels. Uses ChEMBL REST API similarity search + Tanimoto-weighted activity transfer, with descriptor-based fallback. Computes selectivity entropy and Gini index. Input: SMILES + target_class. Output: selectivity_panel.csv, selectivity_metrics.json.

name: covalent_warhead_design
tools_used: RDKit, CovPDB warhead library, Mah 2014 GSH reactivity data
description: Evaluates electrophilic warhead reactivity for targeted covalent inhibitors. Classifies warhead type (acrylamide, chloroacetamide, vinyl sulfone, etc.) via SMARTS, predicts GSH half-life from literature data, and estimates kinome cysteine selectivity. Input: SMILES. Output: warhead_profile.json, cys_selectivity.csv, recommendation.json.

name: pbpk_simulation
tools_used: SciPy LSODA ODE, Rodgers/Rowland Kp model, Willmann physiology database
description: 8-compartment physiologically-based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model (Rodgers/Rowland method). Mechanistic organ-level PK: gut wall, liver (first-pass), blood, lung, kidney, peripheral tissues. Supports healthy adult, pediatric, elderly, and hepatic impairment populations. Input: physicochemical params + CLint + dose. Output: pk_profile.csv, nca_parameters.json.

name: clinical_trial_simulation
tools_used: SciPy, NumPy, BOIN algorithm (Liu & Yuan 2015), 1-cmt PopPK
tags: clinical trial simulation,BOIN,dose escalation,MTD,Phase I,Phase II,PopPK,exposure response,IIV,DLT,oncology dose
description: Simulates Phase I dose escalation and Phase II clinical trials. Supports 3+3 and BOIN (Liu & Yuan 2015) designs. Uses 1-compartment PopPK with log-normal IIV and Emax exposure-response model. Computes MTD operating characteristics and Phase II response rate over n_simulations. Input: dose levels + PK params + ER model. Output: dose_escalation_results.csv, operating_characteristics.json.

name: metabolite_prediction_biotransformer
tools_used: RDKit AllChem, SMARTS reaction rules (BioTransformer3.0 rule-derived)
description: Predicts phase I and phase II metabolites of small molecules using SMARTS-based transformation rules (BioTransformer 3.0 rule-derived). Phase I: aliphatic/aromatic hydroxylation, N-/O-dealkylation, N-oxidation, sulfoxidation, ester/amide hydrolysis, ketone reduction. Phase II: UGT glucuronidation, SULT sulfation, NAT acetylation, GST glutathione conjugation, COMT methylation. Gut microbiota transformations (glucuronide hydrolysis, dehydroxylation). Multi-cycle metabolism (up to 3 generations). Output: metabolites.csv with SMILES, enzyme, confidence, generation; metabolite tree JSON.

name: pharmacogenomics_pgx_report
tools_used: CPIC 2024 guidelines, PharmGKB annotations, star allele activity scoring
description: Generates a pharmacogenomics (PGx) clinical report from diplotype data. Accepts pre-called star alleles for CYP2D6, CYP2C19, CYP2C9, CYP3A5, SLCO1B1, TPMT, DPYD, UGT1A1, VKORC1, CYP2B6, NUDT15. Maps activity scores to CPIC phenotype (Poor/Intermediate/Normal/Ultrarapid Metabolizer). Reports drug-specific dosing recommendations and contraindications per CPIC 2024 guidelines. Flags actionable drug-gene pairs: dose reductions, contraindications, alternative recommendations. Modeled after PharmCAT (Sangkuhl et al. 2021) report structure.

name: herg_cardiac_safety_qsar
tools_used: RDKit, QSAR hERG model (Aronov 2005), ICH E14/S7B framework
tags: hERG,cardiac safety,QTc,ICH E14,ICH S7B,Nav1.5,safety pharmacology,arrhythmia,potassium channel,QSAR
description: Predicts hERG potassium channel inhibition IC50 (µM) and QTc prolongation risk using a physicochemical QSAR model (Aronov 2005; Sanguinetti 2006). Computes ICH E14/S7B safety margin (hERG IC50_free / Cmax_free) and risk tier (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW/MINIMAL). Scans for Nav1.5 structural alerts (class I antiarrhythmic scaffolds) that compound cardiac liability. Input: SMILES, optional measured_hERG_IC50_uM, dose_mg, fup. Output: herg_risk.json, cardiac_safety_summary.csv, nav15_alerts.csv.

name: genotoxicity_ames_prediction
tools_used: RDKit, Derek Nexus-derived SMARTS alerts, ICH S2(R1), Kazius 2005 QSAR
description: Predicts Ames mutagenicity and genotoxicity potential using a structural alert library derived from Derek Nexus rules and ICH S2(R1) guidance (Bailey 2005; Kazius 2005). Covers 3 ICH categories: direct DNA reactants (Category A: nitro aromatics, primary aromatic amines, nitrosamines, epoxides), indirect mutagens via metabolic activation (Category B: PAHs, furans, Michael acceptors, azo dyes), and clastogenic/aneugenic scaffolds (Category C: topo II inhibitors). Recommends ICH S2(R1)-compliant genotoxicity battery for IND filing. Input: SMILES. Output: ames_prediction.json, genotox_alerts.csv, ichs2_summary.json.

name: target_tractability_scorer
tools_used: Oprea TDL 2018, OpenTargets tractability framework, Edfeldt 2011 pocket scoring
description: Scores a protein target's tractability for small molecule and biologic drug discovery. Combines protein family tractability (kinase/GPCR/nuclear receptor = high; PPI/transcription factor = low), pocket druggability (volume/hydrophobicity from fpocket heuristics, Edfeldt 2011), ChEMBL data density (Target Development Level: Tdark/Tbio/Tchem/Tclin, Oprea 2018), and OpenTargets disease association score. Outputs separate SM and biologic tractability scores (0–1) with tier labels and modality recommendation. Input: target_name, protein_class, pocket_volume_A3, chembl_compound_count, has_crystal_structure, disease_association_score. Output: tractability_score.json, evidence_table.csv.

name: pbpk_pediatric_pregnancy
tools_used: SciPy ODE, Bjorkman 2005/Johnson 2006 maturation functions, WHO growth data, Jeong 2012
tags: pediatric PBPK,pregnancy PK,CYP maturation,dose adjustment,allometric scaling,neonatal,CYP3A4 induction,Bjorkman,Jeong 2012
description: Age-stratified PBPK simulation for pediatric dose prediction and pregnancy PK changes. Applies CYP maturation Hill functions (CYP3A4/2D6/2C9/1A2) from Bjorkman 2005 and Johnson 2006, with WHO-based age-scaled organ volumes and cardiac output across 10 age groups (neonate to adult). Simulates pregnancy trimester physiology: plasma volume expansion (+45%), GFR increase (+50% T3), CYP3A4 induction (1.8x T3), CYP2D6 induction (2x T3), CYP1A2 downregulation (0.5x T3) per Jeong 2012/Anger 2014. Generates age-adjusted dose recommendations to match adult AUC target. Input: physicochemical params (MW, logP, CLint, Vss, fup, CYP substrate). Output: pediatric_pk.csv (10 age groups), pregnancy_pk.csv (5 trimesters), dose_recommendation.json.

name: antibody_developability
tools_used: CamSol proxy (Sormanni 2015), Vlasak 2009 deamidation, Deng 2012 FcRn model
description: In silico developability assessment for antibody and biologic drug candidates. Predicts: (1) aggregation propensity using CamSol-inspired hydrophobicity patch scoring (Sormanni 2015) over CDR sequences; (2) deamidation liabilities from NG/NS/DG motifs in CDRs (Vlasak 2009; Yan 2009); (3) oxidation liabilities at Met/Trp/Tyr residues (Houde 2011); (4) isoelectric point (pI) via Henderson-Hasselbalch titration; (5) FcRn-predicted serum half-life from pI (Deng 2012); (6) viscosity risk for SC formulation. Input: full_sequence or CDR sequences (HCDR1/2/3, LCDR1/2/3), antibody_format (IgG1/IgG4/scFv), target_indication. Output: developability_scores.json, liability_scan.csv.

name: hts_plate_qc_hit_calling
tags: HTS,high-throughput screening,Z-factor,hit calling,dose response,4PL,Hill equation,plate QC,Z-prime,IC50
description: High-Throughput Screening (HTS) plate quality control and hit identification. Computes Z-factor and Z'-factor (Zhang 1999) from positive/negative controls. Normalizes raw signals to percent inhibition/activation. Applies configurable hit threshold (default ≥50%) with n-sigma statistics. Fits 4-parameter logistic (4PL/Hill equation) dose-response curves when replicate concentration data are provided (Sebaugh 2011). Accepts plate_data_json array of {well, compound_id, signal, is_pos_ctrl, is_neg_ctrl, concentration_uM} or generates synthetic 96-well demo data. Output: qc_metrics.json (Z', CV, signal window), hit_list.csv, dose_response_curves.csv.

name: exposure_response_modelling
tools_used: SciPy curve_fit, Mager & Jusko 2001, FDA E-R guidance 2019
tags: exposure response,ER modelling,Emax,EC50,Hill equation,PK-PD,dose optimization,FDA ER guidance,Phase I,benefit-risk
description: Fits Emax/Emin exposure-response (E-R) models to clinical or preclinical PK-PD data. Supports Emax (sigmoid Hill equation), linear, and power-law E-R models. Estimates EC50, Emax, Hill coefficient with confidence from SciPy curve_fit. Computes E-R safety margin (TEC / EC50_target) and provides dose recommendations to achieve E50, target effect %, and E90. Follows FDA E-R analysis guidance (2019) for Phase I/II go/no-go decisions and benefit-risk assessment. Input: er_data_json [{exposure_metric, effect, dose_mg}], er_model, target_effect_pct, safety_exposure_uM. Output: er_parameters.json (EC50, Emax, Hill, R²), er_curve.csv, dose_recommendation.json.

name: adaptive_trial_design
tools_used: SciPy, NumPy, Thall & Wathen 2007 RAR, Royston 2011 MAMS, Lan & DeMets 1983
tags: adaptive trial,MAMS,RAR,Thompson sampling,interim analysis,OBrien-Fleming,futility,Phase II,Phase III,dose escalation,operating characteristics
description: Simulates adaptive clinical trial designs for Phase II/III. Implements Response-Adaptive Randomization (RAR) via Thompson sampling (Thall & Wathen 2007) and Multi-Arm Multi-Stage (MAMS) designs with interim analyses (Royston 2011). Applies O'Brien-Fleming efficacy stopping boundaries and Pocock futility stopping (Lan & DeMets 1983 alpha/beta spending). Reports operating characteristics (power, correct arm selection %, early stop rates, mean N enrolled) from Monte Carlo simulation (default 1000 trials). Input: n_arms, true_response_rates, n_interim_analyses, alpha, power, n_simulations, design_type (MAMS | RAR). Output: adaptive_design.json (OC table), arm_allocation.csv, stopping_boundaries.csv.
